title: Omeros beat estimates, Enanta missed on revenue with a target stillimplying 78% upside, and Insight Molecular doubled revenue
author: tickeron_community
selftext:
Today's biotech and healthcare write-ups mix fresh earnings prints  
with some large average targets. Enanta missed on fiscal Q4 revenue  
and still carries a large average target. Revenue bases vary wildly,  
and a couple of targets rest on one or two analysts.  
  
Here is the scorecard from today's write-ups.  
  
\*\*1. Omeros (OMER)\*\* — Adjusted earnings of $0.06 a share beat the  
$0.01 consensus. YARTEMLEA gross revenue climbed to $41.8 million, up  
about 30% from $32.2 million in the prior quarter, with net revenue of  
$35.9 million.  
  
[https://tickeron.com/blogs/omeros-omer-q3-2026-yartemlea-revenue-rises-30-as-adjusted-earnings-top-estimates-39339/](https://tickeron.com/blogs/omeros-omer-q3-2026-yartemlea-revenue-rises-30-as-adjusted-earnings-top-estimates-39339/)  
  
\*\*2. Omeros (OMER)\*\* — The $27.50 target is the average of the two  
most current analyst targets: $22 (Cantor Fitzgerald) and $33 (H.C.  
Wainwright). With OMER last closing near $16.68, that implies about  
65% upside. Target, not a promise.  
  
[https://tickeron.com/blogs/omeros-omer-breaking-down-the-27-50-price-target-and-65-upside-potential-39340/](https://tickeron.com/blogs/omeros-omer-breaking-down-the-27-50-price-target-and-65-upside-potential-39340/)  
  
\*\*3. Enanta Pharmaceuticals (ENTA)\*\* — Fiscal Q4 net loss was $23.7  
million, or $0.81 a share, versus a loss of $18.7 million, or $0.87 a  
share, a year earlier. Quarterly revenue fell to $12.9 million from  
$15.1 million, below a FactSet consensus of about $14.6 million.  
  
[https://tickeron.com/blogs/enanta-pharmaceuticals-enta-delivers-fiscal-2026-results-with-wider-loss-and-extended-cash-runway-39368/](https://tickeron.com/blogs/enanta-pharmaceuticals-enta-delivers-fiscal-2026-results-with-wider-loss-and-extended-cash-runway-39368/)  
  
\*\*4. Enanta Pharmaceuticals (ENTA)\*\* — The $19 target is the average  
of three maintained targets ($20, $20, and $17), consistent with a $19  
average across four firms. From about $10.67, reaching $19 would take  
a gain of about 78%. Target, not a promise.  
  
[https://tickeron.com/blogs/enanta-pharmaceuticals-enta-analyst-19-target-implies-78-upside-39373/](https://tickeron.com/blogs/enanta-pharmaceuticals-enta-analyst-19-target-implies-78-upside-39373/)  
  
\*\*5. Insight Molecular Diagnostics (IMDX)\*\* — Q3 revenue rose to  
$559,000, more than doubling from about $260,000 a year earlier. The  
net loss narrowed to $0.10 a share, beating a $0.24 consensus loss.  
Still a very small revenue base.  
  
[https://tickeron.com/blogs/insight-molecular-diagnostics-imdx-q3-2026-results-sharper-margins-and-narrower-losses-point-to-transition-progress-39402/](https://tickeron.com/blogs/insight-molecular-diagnostics-imdx-q3-2026-results-sharper-margins-and-narrower-losses-point-to-transition-progress-39402/)  
  
\*\*6. IDEXX Laboratories (IDXX)\*\* — Shares gained about 33% over 30  
days, from about $529 to about $704, per the write-up, not a live  
quote. The move followed a Q3 beat and a raised full-year outlook,  
including a roughly 22% single-session jump in early November.  
  
[https://tickeron.com/blogs/idexx-laboratories-idxx-advances-33-on-strong-third-quarter-results-38448/](https://tickeron.com/blogs/idexx-laboratories-idxx-advances-33-on-strong-third-quarter-results-38448/)  
  
\*\*7. Jasper Therapeutics (JSPR)\*\* — Q3 revenue was $8.0 million, the  
first full period after the July Kira Pharmaceuticals deal. The net  
loss was $144.5 million, or $10.19 a share.  
  
[https://tickeron.com/blogs/jasper-therapeutics-jspr-reports-q3-2026-results-following-kira-acquisition-39353/](https://tickeron.com/blogs/jasper-therapeutics-jspr-reports-q3-2026-results-following-kira-acquisition-39353/)  
  
\*\*8. Glass House Brands (GLAS)\*\* — Q3 revenue was $56.8 million, up  
from $47.0 million in Q2 and $26.2 million a year earlier. Biomass  
production hit a record of about 319,000 pounds, and production cost  
fell to about $110 a pound from $122.  
  
[https://tickeron.com/blogs/glass-house-brands-glas-achieves-record-biomass-production-in-q3-2026-39377/](https://tickeron.com/blogs/glass-house-brands-glas-achieves-record-biomass-production-in-q3-2026-39377/)  
  
\*\*9. Precision Optics (POCI)\*\* — The $8 target implies about 61%  
upside from about $4.97, but it is not a consensus — Precision Optics  
has only one published target, plus a prior all-time-high zone near  
$7.85. Target, not a promise.  
  
[https://tickeron.com/blogs/precision-optics-poci-analyzing-the-path-to-an-8-target-and-61-upside-39415/](https://tickeron.com/blogs/precision-optics-poci-analyzing-the-path-to-an-8-target-and-61-upside-39415/)  
  
\*\*10. So-Young International (SY)\*\* — So-Young is expected to report  
Q3 around November 23, before the U.S. open, though the date is not  
officially confirmed. Consensus is a loss of about $0.05 per ADS on  
revenue of about $75.9 million.  
  
[https://tickeron.com/blogs/so-young-international-sy-earnings-preview-strong-clinic-growth-ahead-in-q3-2026-39384/](https://tickeron.com/blogs/so-young-international-sy-earnings-preview-strong-clinic-growth-ahead-in-q3-2026-39384/)  
  
Which healthcare print or target looks most grounded, and which one is  
too thin on coverage or revenue to take seriously?  
  
Not financial advice. Figures are from today's (Nov 16) write-ups,  
using intraday or latest-close prices, not live quotes. Price targets  
are targets, not promises.
